channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: Microsoft introduces new Copilot features and IQ platform at Ignite 2026
item.description: Microsoft announced new AI innovations at Ignite 2026, including Copilot Workspaces, Autopilot, and the Microsoft IQ enterprise context management platform. Volkswagen Group is equipping over 330,000 employees with Copilot. For those following AI, the announcements show how major technology providers are moving past basic chatbots toward persistent agents and enterprise context management systems designed for scale.

item.title: Microsoft and Salesforce announce Copilotforce partnership
item.description: Microsoft and Salesforce announced Copilotforce, a partnership that integrates Salesforce customer context and actions into Microsoft AI tools like Copilot, Teams, and Fabric. The announcement was made on November 17, 2026. This partnership connects CRM data directly with enterprise productivity and AI platforms, allowing businesses to use customer insights inside tools like Microsoft Copilot.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for ChatGPT Work and Codex
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API with improvements in professional outputs, coding, and efficiency. Astra's standard input and output prices are 20 percent lower than the previous version, while Sol offers lower-cost everyday performance. The release updates OpenAI's frontier and everyday models with lower costs and higher efficiency across multiple platforms and subscription tiers.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify before US House committees on Dec 1
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on Dec 1. The hearing follows his resignation amid a scandal involving an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The testimony could shape U.S. policy on AI chip exports and national‑security oversight of leading semiconductor firms.

item.title: AI in gaming: experts warn against single-field narrative
item.description: Ethan Mollick posted on Bluesky that the narrative that games will be the only field where humans write code unassisted is wrong. He argues that this push from press and fans misses an opportunity to guide AI usage to empower workers and help gaming thrive. It highlights the risk of limiting AI adoption in gaming to a narrow role and the need for broader, worker‑empowering approaches.

item.title: Genesis AI raises $500 million Series A at $3.5 billion valuation
item.description: Genesis AI, a Paris‑based robot maker, announced a $500 million Series A round valuing the company at $3.5 billion. The funding will support expanding computing infrastructure, robot production and hiring. The round shows strong investor confidence in robots that learn from human motion, indicating a shift toward more capable automation for warehouses, labs and homes.

item.title: Nvidia unveils Nemotron for Science model and Rubin HPC GPU with 50,000+ CUDA cores at SC26
item.description: At the SC26 supercomputing conference, Nvidia announced the Nemotron for Science open model and the Rubin HPC GPU featuring more than 50,000 CUDA cores. The announcements also included new AI‑agent tools, an expanded Vera CPU platform and a collaboration with IBM on quantum computing. The new model and high‑core GPU aim to accelerate AI‑driven scientific simulations, making large‑scale experiments faster and more accessible.

item.title: Google signs $500M+ geothermal power deal with Quaise Energy in Oregon
item.description: Google signed a deal valued at over $500 million to secure 50 megawatts of geothermal power from Quaise Energy's Project Obsidian in Oregon. The carbon-free energy will support Google's data centers in the state starting as early as 2030. The agreement represents a major commercial commitment by a major tech company to source firm, carbon-free energy from superhot geothermal technology for power-hungry data centers.

item.title: Anthropic grants METR employee-level access to its AI models and safety tools
item.description: Anthropic gave six METR researchers company laptops, office space and internal tool access to evaluate its frontier AI models, safety practices and risk management. Deep external access lets independent evaluators scrutinize Anthropic’s systems, addressing concerns about AI safety and transparency.

item.title: HCLTech and Cohere partner to build sovereign AI solutions
item.description: HCLTech and Cohere have partnered to build and deliver sovereign artificial intelligence solutions for enterprises and governments in Canada and Germany. The initial development targets insurance, financial services, and manufacturing. This partnership expands enterprise access to sovereign AI platforms, allowing regulated industries to deploy AI tools while meeting local data residency and security requirements.

item.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion Series C to speed AI‑driven drug trials
item.description: Alphabet’s Isomorphic Labs announced a $5 billion Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital and Greenoaks. The money will expand its IsoDDE AI drug‑design engine and move candidates toward clinical trials. The funding accelerates the use of AI to design and test new medicines, a key step toward faster, cheaper drug development.

item.title: Dreamteam raises $53m to build AI-native CRM with AI teammates
item.description: Dreamteam raised $53 million across seed and Series A rounds to build an AI-native CRM platform featuring AI teammates that manage sales workflows. The startup has signed up over 100 companies across 13 countries. The funding highlights growing venture capital interest in enterprise AI startups attempting to disrupt established CRM software categories dominated by companies like Salesforce and HubSpot.

item.title: Chinese records show Kang Wei built state-backed data center network
item.description: Chinese records show Alice Huang's husband, Kang Wei, built a state-backed data center network in China with proposed investments exceeding $9 billion between 2021 and 2024. U.S. President Donald Trump stated that he does not believe national security was put at risk by former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang. The disclosures highlight ongoing government scrutiny surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang amid U.S. export controls on chips to China.

item.title: Nvidia board creates National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
item.description: Nvidia's board of directors established a new standing committee to oversee the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management. The committee, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, will meet at least quarterly and retain independent outside experts. Elevating export control oversight to board level signals that chip export restrictions are a top regulatory risk for Nvidia and its industry.

item.title: Sarvam AI opens Token Factory to run global open-weight models on Indian servers
item.description: Sarvam AI launched Token Factory, an OpenAI-compatible API that serves its Sarvam 105B model and global open-weight models (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Gemma) on GPU clusters in India, charging by usage. The company says it already serves more than 450 billion DeepSeek V4.1 Flash tokens a day. Sarvam's entry adds a domestic, usage-priced option for running global open-weight models in India, intensifying competition in a local inference market that already includes Krutrim, OpenAI and Anthropic.

item.title: Numa raises $45M Series C to expand AI operating system for car dealerships
item.description: Oakland‑based Numa secured $45 million in a Series C round led by Blue Cloud Ventures, bringing total funding to $96 million and a post‑money valuation of $500 million. The company now serves more than 1,500 dealerships in the U.S. and Canada. The funding shows that AI solutions for legacy industries like automotive retail are attracting significant investment and scaling rapidly.

item.title: OpenAI names Pragya Misra to lead business development in India and South Asia
item.description: Pragya Misra, OpenAI's head of strategy and global affairs in India, will take on a new role leading the company's business development for India and South Asia. She joined OpenAI in April 2024 as its first hire in India, and the company says India is its largest market with over 100 million weekly users. The appointment signals OpenAI's intent to deepen commercial partnerships in its largest market as it prepares for an IPO.

item.title: US tightens AI chip export rules, targeting Southeast Asia data centres
item.description: The US Commerce Department announced new export controls on Nov 16 requiring licenses for AI chip shipments to data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil that may provide compute to Chinese firms. Shares of Southeast Asian data centre and chip supply chain companies fell sharply, with some Malaysian firms dropping nearly 20%. The rules close a major loophole that allowed Chinese AI companies to access advanced US computing power through overseas data centres, reshaping the global AI compute landscape and imposing new compliance burdens on Southeast Asian data centre operators.

item.title: Review shows AI distillation moving to industrial use in China
item.description: A review of over 300 Chinese documents shows that AI distillation has moved from academic experiments to widespread industrial use. Chinese entities are adopting sophisticated ways to use output from leading American AI models to train domestic rivals. The widespread industrial use of AI distillation in China potentially weakens U.S. efforts to contain Beijing's technological rise through semiconductor export restrictions.

item.title: US Commerce Dept and DOJ investigated Megaspeed over chip exports in 2024
item.description: The U.S. Commerce Department and Department of Justice investigated Singapore-based Megaspeed starting in 2024 over potential export violations regarding Nvidia chips. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its no-sell list in June 2025. The joint investigation highlights ongoing U.S. enforcement actions surrounding the diversion of advanced AI hardware to restricted markets.

item.title: Amazon's Ohio data center plans face risks after voter restrictions
item.description: Amazon's planned investments of over $17 billion in Ohio data centers are at risk after midterm voters passed restriction measures affecting proposed projects. Voters in Sunbury, Ohio, approved a ban on large data centers in the November 3 election, raising obstacles for Amazon's proposed US$2 billion project. It highlights how local community opposition and ballot measures are increasingly threatening major tech infrastructure expansion and AI investments across the United States.

item.title: Meta modifies Instagram recommendation systems in India to curb violent content
item.description: Meta modified Instagram's recommendation systems in India to reduce sexually suggestive and violent content from accounts users do not follow. The updates use advanced AI models to filter content proactively across Reels, Explore, and Feed following regulatory scrutiny. This development shows how social media platforms adjust their content algorithms in response to increased regulatory oversight in major markets.

item.title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos ported to AMD GPUs in three days with almost no human work
item.description: Anthropic told investors its Claude Mythos Preview model was running on AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days, writing almost all the low‑level kernels itself, a task that previously took six to twelve months. The speed of hardware onboarding could let AI providers switch chips without long engineering delays, challenging Nvidia’s long‑standing software advantage.

item.title: OpenAI study finds 98% of scientists expect AI to accelerate research
item.description: An OpenAI study found that 98 per cent of surveyed scientists expect artificial intelligence to accelerate discoveries in their fields. The research analyzed 580,186 scientific messages from 1,819 researchers and a survey of 251 participants using ChatGPT. The study provides empirical data on how academic researchers actually integrate AI tools into their workflows, highlighting heavy use in writing and reading alongside persistent bottlenecks like funding and staffing.

item.title: macOS 27.3 beta adds privacy controls for AI apps and full disk access
item.description: Apple released the macOS 27.3 beta, splitting the device control setting into two categories and adding restricted folder permissions to address security risks from AI agents. The update introduces a menu bar indicator and prompts users to select specific apps for automation tools to control. The update changes how AI agents and automation tools request and receive system-level permissions on macOS.

item.title: Ethan Mollick on computer infrastructure and offensive AI threats
item.description: Ethan Mollick noted that computer infrastructure is an improvised system vulnerable to cascading failures and outlined the arrival of offensive AI threats alongside defensive AIs and patching. It highlights the growing security concerns surrounding the intersection of fragile computer infrastructure and emerging offensive AI capabilities.

item.title: OpenAI collaborates with NATO and allied cyber agencies on AI defense
item.description: OpenAI is working with NATO and allied cyber agencies to help trusted defenders find vulnerabilities, test fixes, and protect essential systems using AI. The collaboration highlights the increasing use of artificial intelligence in national security and government cyber defense operations.

item.title: Nvidia introduces DGX Spark HPC developer kit for desks
item.description: Nvidia introduced the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit at SC26, providing a four-node cluster that fits on a desk for researchers and developers. The kit features the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip and provides 512GB of combined memory and 20TB of NVMe storage. This developer kit gives researchers direct desktop access to multi-node computing power for AI and scientific workloads, eliminating the need to wait for shared GPU cluster time.

item.title: Nvidia faces third-quarter earnings call under interim CEO Colette Kress
item.description: Nvidia reports its third-quarter results with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO following the resignation of founder Jensen Huang. The company faces congressional inquiries and questions regarding chip sales to China and export restrictions. As the dominant provider of AI hardware infrastructure, Nvidia's leadership transition and regulatory scrutiny directly impact the broader artificial intelligence industry's supply chain and market stability.

item.title: India and nine nations sign declaration to safeguard AI supply chains
item.description: India and nine other nations signed the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity to protect AI infrastructure and sensitive technologies. The agreement was signed on November 15 at the Pax Silica retreat. The agreement sets up international cooperation between ten nations to secure AI supply chains, address market-distorting policies, and establish working groups for technology resilience.
